artists.biography:
Elvis Costello (born Declan Patrick MacManus, 25 August 1954) is an English singer-songwriter. He began his career as part of London's pub rock scene in the early-1970s and later became associated with the first wave of the British Punk/New Wave movement of the mid to late-1970s. Steeped in word play, the vocabulary of Costello's lyrics is broader than that of most popular songs. His music has drawn on many diverse genres; one critic described him as a "pop encyclopaedia", able to "reinvent the past in his own image".

Costello has won multiple awards in his career, including a Grammy Award, and has twice been nominated for the Brit Award for Best British Male. In 2003, Elvis Costello & the Attractions were inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame. In 2004, Rolling Stone ranked Costello number 80 on their list of the 100 Greatest Artists of All Time.

perplexity.description:
The Man: The Best of Elvis Costello, released in 1986 by Demon Records, is a career-spanning compilation that showcases the breadth of Elvis Costello's early work, primarily focusing on his output from the late 1970s through the mid-1980s. The album features a mix of sharp, new wave-inflected rock, power pop, and soulful balladry, highlighting Costello's signature blend of lyrical wit, emotional intensity, and musical versatility. Tracks such as "Watching the Detectives," "Oliver's Army," "Alison," and "Accidents Will Happen" exemplify his knack for merging catchy melodies with biting social commentary and introspective storytelling.

This compilation holds a significant place in Costello's discography as one of the first major retrospectives of his career, capturing the evolution of his sound from the raw energy of his debut My Aim Is True to the more sophisticated arrangements of albums like Imperial Bedroom. While it was released after several other compilations, including the 1985 US release The Best of Elvis Costello and the Attractions, The Man offered a distinct track selection tailored for the UK market. The album received generally positive attention for its curation, though it was not as widely reviewed as some of Costello's studio albums; it remains a respected entry point for new listeners and a concise summary of his influential early period.
